verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Fade the Bounce; CPI Wednesday Is the Only Binary That Matters
verdict.rationale_short: Monday opens with a modest AI-driven NQ relief bounce (+0.6% futures, NVDA recovery at $214, MRVL +7%) but the macro regime has not improved — it has worsened. Iran and Israel exchanged missiles overnight, pushing Brent above $97 and breaching the prior briefing's oil trigger. AMD is -10.86% and TSM -6.69%, confirming no broad semi recovery; only the NVDA ecosystem is bid. Three regime triggers remain breached (VIX above 18, SPX below 7,460, Brent above $97), and CPI Wednesday carries a 67% probability of a hot print above 4.2% YoY. Hold cash, maintain the IWM short, cover any lingering XLE stub above $97, and let Wednesday decide.

bear_case: Monday's AI-driven NQ bounce is a single-catalyst event masking a deteriorating macro regime. The Iran-Israel missile exchange overnight sent Brent above $97 — the prior briefing's trigger level — adding a direct inflationary multiplier to a CPI print that prediction markets already price at 67% probability above 4.2% YoY. AMD's -10.86% session confirms no broad semi recovery; only the NVDA ecosystem is bid, and that is a narrative trade in a rate-hostile environment, not a regime change. SPX remains below 7,460, VIX remains above 18, and the 30Y has not broken below 5.0%. If CPI prints hot on Wednesday, the June 17 Warsh FOMC becomes a live hike, the 30Y targets 5.10-5.20%, and SPX 7,250 is the next meaningful support. Invalidation level: a cool CPI (core ≤0.2% m/m) with SPX closing above 7,460 and VIX back below 17 converts the call to HOLD.
